description:
How to Apply for a Master's or PhD in the UK (Official Links)

Direct answer box (first 50 words):

Taught Master's in the UK apply either through UCAS Postgraduate or directly on each university's portal; PhDs apply directly to departments — usually by emailing a prospective supervisor with a research proposal first. Deadlines for 2027 entry mostly fall between October 2026 and June 2027, with funded places closing earliest.

The application system in one paragraph

The UK has no single postgraduate application system. Taught Master's programmes increasingly use UCAS Postgraduate, but many universities still use their own portals — always check the course page. PhD applications are always direct to the department, and the real first step is informal: identifying and contacting a supervisor. Everything else — proposals, references, interviews — hangs off that skeleton. Start from our 12-month application timeline so the sequencing is right from month one.

Step 1 — Choose your programmes (and read the entry requirements properly)

Shortlist 4–6 programmes rather than 20. For each, verify:

  • Entry requirements: a 2:1 UK Bachelor's or international equivalent is standard for Master's; PhDs often want a Master's at Merit level or a strong Bachelor's. If your grades came out of a different system, our CGPA to UK degree classification guide explains how admissions convert them.
  • English requirements: typically IELTS 6.5–7.0 overall for Master's, 7.0 for competitive programmes; requirements vary by department. Compare tests in our IELTS vs TOEFL vs PTE for UK PhDs guide — most universities accept all three.
  • Funding status: a PhD place without funding is a different decision from a funded one. See how to identify PhDs that are really funded for international students before you fall in love with a project.

Step 2 — For PhDs: contact supervisors before you apply

This step separates successful PhD applicants from rejected ones:

  1. Find the right person. Search department pages for staff whose recent publications genuinely overlap with your proposal — not just keyword matches.
  2. Email them properly. A short, specific email: who you are, what you propose, why them, and what you have attached. Our 7 email templates for PhD supervisors gives you exact wording, and the follow-up guide covers what to do when supervisors don't reply.
  3. Expect three outcomes: an invitation to apply formally (good), a redirect to a colleague (also good), or silence (move on after one polite follow-up).

Many UK PhD projects are advertised positions — for those, apply directly to the advert. Reading the advert carefully changes how you should apply: see our how to read a PhD job advertisement guide.

Step 3 — Prepare your documents

Give referees 4–6 weeks' notice and send them your CV and statement — a briefed referee writes a far better letter.

Step 4 — Apply through the right portal

  • UCAS Postgraduate (ucas.com): used by many universities for taught Master's. One profile, one personal statement per choice, application fee applies.
  • University direct portals: each university's postgraduate admissions page hosts its own form — search "[university name] postgraduate application". Create accounts early; transcripts often need manual upload.
  • PhD applications: the department's "how to apply" page specifies whether you email the supervisor first or submit to a portal with them named. Follow the stated order exactly.
  • Oxbridge and medicine-adjacent programmes: earlier deadlines (often October–January) and extra documents. Check the specific course page — these differ from everything else.

Step 5 — Secure funding in parallel

Do not wait for an offer before applying for funding; most schemes require (or favour) simultaneous applications:

Interviews are part of PhD selection at most universities — prepare with our PhD interview questions and answers guide.

Frequently asked questions

Do I use UCAS for a PhD in the UK? No. PhDs apply directly to the university department, usually after supervisor contact. UCAS Postgraduate serves taught Master's programmes at participating universities only.

When should I start applying for 2027 entry? Begin researching and contacting supervisors 12–18 months ahead — mid-2026 for autumn 2027. Funded places and scholarships close earliest, often by December or January.

Can I apply for a UK PhD without a Master's? Sometimes — UK programmes frequently accept exceptional Bachelor's graduates directly, especially in the sciences. It depends on the department. Our PhD without a Master's guide explains when it works.

Is it harder for international students to get UK PhD funding? Yes for some schemes — many UKRI studentships reserve or limit places by fee status, though fully open international schemes exist and are growing. Target them deliberately using our identifying funded PhDs guide.

Official source

Application processes, deadlines and fee statuses vary by university and change each cycle. Always verify requirements on the official course page (university website) and ucas.com before applying — this guide orients you, but the course page rules.
